title: Move-Then-Operate: Behavioral Phasing for Human-Like Robotic Manipulation
claim: Manipulation alternates between fast coarse relocation and slow fine-grained contact phases, so a single monolithic policy conflates two distinct regimes.
layout: 2x3 grid of frames, snaking left-to-right then right-to-left, with a connecting arrow
description: A six-frame storyboard of a dual-arm robot picking up food items and placing them on a tray. Frames are arranged in two rows of three, linked by an orange arrow that runs left to right along the top row, curves down at the right edge, and runs right to left along the bottom row. Each frame has a hand-drawn border and a title: 'Phase: Move' with a rocket emoji in red-bordered frames, and 'Phase: Operate' with a monocle-face emoji in blue-bordered frames. Frames overlay semi-transparent ghosted arm positions. The Move frames show large, blurred arm displacements. The Operate frames show tighter, near-stationary arm poses around the objects. The eye goes first to the alternating red and blue frames and the emoji labels.
caption: Schematic of robotic manipulation phases via equidistant sampling. The sequence comprises a fast and rapid move phase characterized by large displacements, and an operate phase focused on fine-grained and tenuous precision.
abstract: We present Move-Then-Operate, a Vision language action framework that explicitly decouples robotic manipulation into two distinct behavioral phases: coarse relocation (move) and contact-critical interaction (operate). Unlike monolithic policies that conflate these heterogeneous regimes, our architecture employs a dual-expert policy routed by a learnable phase selector, introducing a structural inductive bias that isolates phase-specific dynamics. Phase labels are automatically generated via an MLLM-based pipeline conditioned on lightweight contextual cues such as end-effector velocity and subtask decomposition to ensure alignment with human motor patterns. Evaluated on the RoboTwin2 benchmark, our method achieves an average success rate of $68.9\%$, outperforming the monolithic $Ï_0$ baseline by $24\%$. It matches or exceeds models trained on $10\times$ more data and reaches peak performance in $40\%$ fewer training steps, demonstrating that architectural disentanglement of move and operate phases is a highly effective and efficient strategy for mastering high-precision manipulation. The code is available at: https://github.com/healenrens/Move-then-Operate
